slides.texte_overlay:
How to sound smart
every time you speak
Use precise words instead of vague ones. Not "it was good" but "it was surprisingly moving." Precision makes you sound thoughtful without trying.
Ask before you assume. "What do you mean by that?" Smart people clarify instead of guessing, and it makes conversations much better.
Admit what you don't know. "I'm not sure, but I think..." Honesty about limits makes everything else you say more believable. It makes people listen closer.
Connect ideas from different areas. A sports lesson for business, a history story for relationships. Unexpected links sound brilliant.
Build your general knowledge. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and it gives me examples to use in almost every conversation.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. It gives me examples to use in almost every conversation.

slides.texte_overlay: Speak a little less than you want to. Short answers leave room for questions. People think you know more when you don't empty everything at once.
Summarise what the other person said. "So your point is..." It shows you understood, and it makes you sound calm and sharp. Then add your own view.
